title: Mix-up attack (RFC 9700, section 4.4)
desc: Three parties: a client that talks to two or more authorization servers, a hostile AS and an honest AS. Step 1: the client starts a flow with the hostile AS. Step 2: the hostile AS redirects the user to the honest AS using the honest client's ID. Step 3: the code returns to the client, which believes it came from the hostile AS. Step 4: the client redeems it at the hostile token endpoint. Defences: the client stores, per request, the issuer it sent the request to, bound to the user agent, because storing only the AS URL is insufficient; and with issuer identification (RFC 9207) it compares the iss in the response with the stored issuer and aborts on a mismatch.
